title: Polylogarithmic-space streaming Euclidean MST estimation
formal:
Does there exist a uniform randomized one-pass insertion-only streaming algorithm A and absolute constants \(C\ge1\), \(K\ge1\) and integer \(k\ge1\) such that, for every \(n\ge2\), \(d\ge1\), \(\Delta\ge2\), and every stream of n distinct points in \(\{0,\ldots,\Delta\}^{d}\), A uses at most
\[K\bigl(d\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\lceil\log_2(\Delta+2)\rceil\bigr)^k\]
bits of working memory and returns a rational estimate Z satisfying
\[\Pr[\operatorname{MST}(X)\le Z\le C\operatorname{MST}(X)]\ge 2/3?\]
The stream order is arbitrary and fixed independently of the algorithm’s private random bits. The output estimates total Euclidean MST cost; it need not describe a tree. For polynomially bounded integer coordinates, the required space is \(\mathrm{poly}(d\log n)\), as in the community proposal.
definitions:
The point set X consists of the n distinct inserted vectors. Coordinates are nonnegative integers given in binary, and the parameters n,d and the bound \(\Delta\) are supplied before the stream. The graph is complete on X; an edge between x and y has weight \(\|x-y\|_2=(\sum_{j=1}^{d}(x_j-y_j)^2)^{1/2}\). The quantity \(\operatorname{MST}(X)\) is the minimum sum of edge weights over all spanning trees of this graph. It is a real number even though the input coordinates are integers.

The algorithm is one fixed finite probabilistic Turing-machine program with a read-once input stream, private independent fair random bits, working tapes, and an output tape used only for the final rational estimate. An input record may be buffered, with those bits charged to memory. All retained state, counters, random seeds and postprocessing workspace count toward the space bound, on every input and every random tape. Consumed input cannot be revisited, and there are no deletions, extra passes, random-order promise, external storage, nonuniform advice or real-number registers. The machine must halt on every random tape; no separate update-time or total-time bound is imposed. The probability is over its coins for each fixed stream. The constants and exponent do not depend on n,d or the coordinate bound.

Dependence polynomial in the bit length of coordinates makes the finite-input convention explicit. In particular, for each fixed integer b and \(\Delta\le n^b\), the bound has the proposal’s \(\mathrm{poly}(d\log n)\) form. The logarithmic coordinate factor is recorded rather than silently treating arbitrary reals as constant-size words. The target allows d to grow, including \(d=\Theta(\log n)\); a bound exponential in d does not qualify. The approximation constant can be any fixed finite C. Requiring the estimate to lie above the true cost is a normalization: a two-sided constant-factor estimate can be rescaled at the cost of changing C. Neither an explicit tree nor a \(1+\varepsilon\) approximation is required.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of existence of an algorithm satisfying the stated memory, pass and probability bounds for some absolute finite approximation constant, or prove the negation for every such algorithm and constants. An \(n^{\varepsilon}\)-space algorithm for a fixed positive \(\varepsilon\), a factor growing with n, a multiple-pass algorithm, or a lower bound excluding only constants near 1 does not settle this target.
why: An MST measures the cost of connecting an entire geometric data set. A small summary that estimates this global quantity within a constant factor would clarify how much connectivity information survives a single streaming pass as dimension grows.

context_blocks.text: Pavel Veselý proposed the insertion-only, one-pass, constant-factor question through the Atlas website. The requested output is the cost of the Euclidean minimum spanning tree, with memory polynomial in dimension and logarithmic in the number of points. This card adds the finite-coordinate, randomness and output conventions needed to make that request precise.

The STOC 2023 paper obtains constant-factor estimation using \(n^{O(\varepsilon)}\) space for a fixed positive parameter \(\varepsilon\). Its sketches support insertions and deletions. This leaves a gap to polylogarithmic memory even in the insertion-only model selected here.

The same paper rules out one-pass space \(o(\sqrt n)\) for approximation better than 1.1035 in sufficiently high dimension. This near-one barrier does not exclude every absolute approximation constant. Its multiple-pass improvements also do not settle the one-pass target.

progress.text: Constant-factor sublinear-space estimation and a near-one approximation lower bound are established; neither supplies the proposed polylogarithmic-space constant-factor algorithm.

status_note: Reviewed on 14 September 2026 against the submitted proposal and the cited paper’s author preprint. A bounded search for subsequent geometric-streaming MST results did not verify a resolution of this insertion-only polylogarithmic-space target. Status remains source_open; this is not an exhaustive literature audit or independent verification of the cited proofs.
review_note: Community proposal developed individually. The finite-coordinate convention and success probability are explicit editorial specifications; the main one-pass insertion-only cost-estimation target is retained.

importance.reason: A general space-versus-approximation barrier for a central geometric connectivity objective, separating polynomially small summaries from polylogarithmic ones as dimension grows.

category_assignment.reason: The main resource is single-pass streaming memory; geometry supplies the input metric, not a separate computational model.

notes: Retained the community proposal’s insertion-only, one-pass, constant-factor target.
Specified finite grid coordinates, all-input success probability, counted workspace and a rational scalar output.
Distinguished n-to-a-positive-power space and near-one lower bounds from the requested polylogarithmic memory.
statement_review.scope: Individual source and formulation review; no proof-assistant formalization.

sentences: Points arrive one at a time in Euclidean space, and the goal is to estimate the cost of connecting them by a minimum spanning tree.
The algorithm gets one insertion-only pass and may keep only memory polynomial in the dimension and the logarithmic input parameters.
It should return a constant-factor estimate with probability at least two thirds for every input order.
The cited paper leaves a gap between its sublinear-space constant-factor result and this smaller memory budget.
The question asks how compactly one can summarize global geometric connectivity, without requiring the summary to output the tree itself.

### Problem statement

Goal: Design an $O(1)$-approximation insertion-only streaming algorithm for estimating the minimum spanning tree (MST) cost in the $d$-dimension Euclidean space using one pass and space $\mathrm{poly}(d\cdot \log n)$, where $n$ is the number of points in the stream. (The dimension $d$ can be assumed to be logarithmic in $n$.)
